draft.title: Fitness testing
card: A fitness test measures one component of fitness using a set method. The result can be compared over time.
a 20 m shuttle run that gets faster each minute. It measures aerobic fitness, and the score is the level and shuttle reached.
reaching forward along a box while seated with straight legs. It measures flexibility of the lower back and hamstrings.
jumping as high as possible from standing and recording the height gained. It measures power in the legs.
draft.remember: Match the test to the component, then repeat it the same way to track change.

a.q: Which component of fitness does the vertical jump test measure?
opts: Leg power
Aerobic fitness
Flexibility of the hamstrings
Running speed over 20 m
a.why: The vertical jump records how high a person can jump, which shows how much force the legs can produce quickly. The beep test is a tempting wrong choice, but it measures aerobic fitness through a running task.
a.clue: Think about what the height of a jump shows about the legs.

b.q: Jin wants to find out how flexible his hamstrings and lower back are. Which test should he use?
opts: Sit and reach
Beep test
Vertical jump
Repeated beep test
b.why: The sit and reach measures flexibility of the lower back and hamstrings. The beep test is wrong because it measures aerobic fitness, not flexibility.
b.clue: Which test involves reaching forward while seated?

proposal.title: Fitness testing
card: A fitness test measures one component of fitness. A test at the start of a program gives a baseline score, and retesting later shows progress.
The beep test, a 20 m shuttle run that gets faster, measures aerobic fitness. The sit and reach measures lower back and hamstring flexibility. The vertical jump measures leg power.
a test is valid if it measures the component it claims to. The sit and reach is valid for hamstring flexibility, but not for leg power.
a test is reliable if it gives similar results when repeated in the same conditions. Changing the warm-up, surface, equipment or tester can make results unreliable.
proposal.remember: Choose a test that measures the right component, then repeat it the same way each time.

a.q: A coach uses the beep test to judge a sprinter's leg power. What is the main problem with this choice?
opts: The test is not valid for leg power
The test is not reliable when repeated
The test cannot give a baseline score
The test measures flexibility instead
a.why: The beep test measures aerobic fitness, so it does not measure leg power and is not valid for that purpose. Reliability is about getting consistent results when the test is repeated, which is not the issue here.
a.clue: Does the test measure what the coach wants to know?

b.q: Ella did the vertical jump in week 1 indoors after a full warm-up. In week 8 she did it on grass with no warm-up and scored lower. What should her coach conclude?
opts: The conditions changed, so the drop may not be real
Her leg power has fallen, so her training failed
The vertical jump is not a valid test of leg power
Her aerobic fitness has dropped since week 1
b.why: The surface and warm-up changed between tests, so the results are not reliable and the lower score may come from the conditions rather than a real loss of power. The vertical jump is still a valid test of leg power, so the problem is reliability, not validity.
b.clue: What changed between the two tests apart from her training?
